title: Keeping hope in a simple ritual
meaning: A tradition can sustain hope for pleasant time together when waiting for complete preparation leaves room for pleasure in the present.
text: A pleasant shared ritual can remind you beforehand that time for each other will be available. The Hierophant in the physical position of Svadhisthana describes a familiar form: a repeated meeting, a favourite arrangement and an activity with a clear beginning. The World in energy leans towards perfectly finished preparations before enjoyment is permitted. The Star in emotions allows hope and inspiration about future closeness. Tradition already offers an invitation, but the demand for a complete whole leaves it waiting. Anticipation can outlast the actual opportunity to spend a pleasant evening together.

For example, you imagine a familiar evening of favourite poems. First, you want a complete selection, beautifully printed pages and suitable music. **Hope for shared pleasure needs only a small living beginning.** You can read one chosen poem and sit beside the impression it leaves. The ritual survives a modest scale, while inspiration gains support from experience already shared, alongside the imagined perfect meeting.

The difficulty is protecting a lovely possibility from every imperfect performance. You add to the selection, postpone the evening and feel true enjoyment is just a little further away. That distance never shrinks. Complete preparation becomes a condition that keeps growing. Shared hope benefits from experience small enough for today. Tradition retains meaning when you can freely live it before the imagined whole receives its final touch.
